title: Rockin' in Rhythm and Harry James's Pecking
summary: Cootie's solo on Rockin' in Rhythm was taken by Harry James as a song he got no credit for; Rockin' in Rhythm came out of Pigmeat Markham rehearsal.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: And wrote. Yeah. Okay, good. Well, listen, now, in November that year, the band made "Rockin' in Rhythm", which was one of the real beautiful numbers, I think. Don't you? Don't you like that number? Or do you think it's too simple?
It was a simple number. Just a simple thing.
It's a simple [blues ], isn't it?
Yeah.
But it has a beautiful swing to it. Don't you think it does? What are you smiling for? What's your feeling about that number? Does it bore you?
No. Well, you know my solo was taken off of that and made another song.
Oh, no. I don't. Which is that?
I think Harry James taken it. And made a song called "Pecking".
No. Really?
Yeah.
I didn't know that. No, I didn't. How about that. So that's what I'm talking about when I say you do a solo that's like a song. How about that. Is that right? And no acknowledgement, no nothing.
No. And I didn't get a dime for it. I don't know if Irving Mills got paid for it.
How about that.
And I --
No lyrics went on that did they?
No.
But it was just one of Harry's trumpet numbers.
Yeah. I don't know if Duke was in on it or not.
(Laughter)
You mean you wonder, huh? Well, how about that. Because it was acknowledged then that it was. Harry acknowledged that that was what he had done, huh? Or that that's what it was, huh?
Everyone knew it.
Everybody knew it.
Because that was my solo, my plain solo, 'Rockin' in Rhythm', he'd taken that and made a song out of it.
(Laughter)
No changes?
No, no changes.
(Laughter)
Oh, isn't that something. Well, listen, my memory of 'Rockin' in Rhythm' particularly is that that was the background for Bessie Dudley's dance act with the band in
theaters. Remember?
Yeah. I think the thing came about, it was Pigmeat Markham.
Yeah.
He was playing in Philadelphia, and during rehearsals, we had to get some music for him. And they started to jiving around, and that's how "Rockin' in Rhythm" came about.
Is it really? So it was born to back up a dancer, then.
Yeah, I think it was.
Yeah. That's what it was.
Yeah. I think it was Harry Carney started playing or something. Somebody. And that's how it came about.
Yeah, because the saxophones are very -- that first chorus is saxophones, isn't it?
I don't recall.
Yeah. I think. Yeah, well, I know that Duke turned -- every time that he wanted to get something going and get it swinging, you know, on stage, he put that in, didn't he?
Yeah. During rehearsal. That's how I remember it came about. Then it just worked itself in.
